slides.kicker: MOST PEOPLE JUST ASK FOR SUMMARIES
slides.image_prompt: SUBJECT: Sundar Pichai, arms wrapped around glowing research papers, delighted grin, sparkling eyes. BACKDROP: bright library shelves, white overhead light, Gemini logo backlit sign. PALETTE: bright Gemini blue, white. Documentary photo, 35mm, natural skin texture, film grain.

slides.headline: 1) CATCH EVERY CONFLICT HIDING ACROSS YOUR SOURCES
slides.body:
A human research assistant flags where sources clash. This prompt does it in under a minute.

"Find every contradiction. For each conflict, name which argument has stronger evidence and why."

slides.headline: 2) TURN 50 PAGES OF RESEARCH INTO ONE BRIEFING
slides.body:
A strategy consultant charges $300 an hour for this. This prompt gets it done in 90 seconds.

"Write a briefing: the 3 key facts, the biggest risk, and the one action to take first."

slides.headline: 3) MAKE IT PREDICT EVERY OBJECTION BEFORE YOUR MEETING
slides.body:
A prep coach charges $200 an hour to stress-test your pitch. This prompt does it for free.

"List the 3 strongest arguments AGAINST my position, with evidence and a two-sentence counter-response for each."

slides.headline: 4) FIND EVERY HIDDEN CONNECTION ACROSS ALL YOUR DOCUMENTS
slides.body:
You read documents one at a time and miss what connects them. Gemini reads all at once.

"Find the 5 most surprising connections: the two sources linked, what they share, and why it matters."

slides.headline: SAVE THIS: 4 GEMINI NOTEBOOK PROMPTS THAT BEAT SUMMARIES
slides.body:

Daily AI news + real skills

caption:
Swipe and save. 4 Gemini Notebook prompts that turn your documents into a personal researcher. 📋

1) Catch every conflict hiding across your sources,
2) Turn 50 pages into a one-page decision briefing,
3) Make it predict every objection before your meeting,
4) Find hidden connections across all your documents at once.

Most people type "summarize this" into Gemini Notebook and stop there. These 4 prompts treat it as a research analyst: finding conflicts, writing briefings, predicting objections, mapping hidden connections. The gap between how most people use this tool and how it can be used is enormous.
